If GtG is going to branch out with the card game, I'd personally rather they do something a little different-er.  I've already got boxes full of superhero decks. I don't need more of those.  But a card game in another genre which is based on the SotM engine but which adds the ability for space marines to swap between vehicles during a fight, or a card game that's a tournament between martial artists using various fighting styles, or a fantasy card game where my character is commanding an army of orcs/elves/dragons... now that's something that gets me excited.

The things about SotM that I would want kept -- gotta be co-op, gotta have a central character for each deck for me to identify with, each deck's gotta feel/play differently from each other.  But it doesn't gotta be superheroes.  We already have that.

[Double edit: the more I think about it, the more I desperately want to play these card games.  Where's the Kickstarter for these?? Sign me up!]

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
The mechanics of Sentinels is pretty much geared strongly towards beings who have inherent powers of some type, I feel. So, superhumans, fantasy beings with magic abilities, science heroes/villains with gadgets or genetic or psionic abilities.

And out of the existing properties that fit those various categories with a good already established fanbase (extremely helpful for trying to spread beyond your own existing audience with a new concept) that don't already have their own card game spinoffs in the pipeline (therein lies the kicker; a lot of notable franchises in the tabletop games genre already have their own in-house board games), Mutants and Masterminds is a pretty good first fit IMHO.

Don't forget also that Christopher and Adam clearly have a specific love for superheroes and comics which might influence things.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
I linked this earlier, but here it is again:

https://freeronin.com/2e_files/FC-encyclopedia.pdf

So we have:

  • Bowman: Fletcher Beaumont III, archer.  Original Bowman was a newspaper reporter, not sure what else his deal is.
  • Captain Thunder: Ray Gardener, controls electricity, flies, and has super strength (and I assume is super tough).  A former test pilot.
  • Daedalus: The actual mythological character.  Wears a mecha suit based on gravity manipulation.
  • Dr. Metropolis: The "Spirit of Cities", sort of a druid but for urban environments, I guess?
  • Johnny Rocket: John Wade II, speedster.  John Wade I was a lab assistant.
  • Lady Liberty: Beth Walton-Wright, Wields the "Light of Liberty," whatever that means.
  • Pseudo: R'ik Faax, a rogue Grue.  Grue are shape-shifting telepathic aliens from Gruen-Prime.
  • The Raven: Callie Summers.  No powers, no background except that she was trained by the first Raven, her dark-clad father.
  • Siren: Cassandra Vale, voodoo sea goddess.
  • Star Knight: Patrick O'Duffy, er, star knight.  They seem to basically be mechanically Iron Man, thematically Green Lantern.  Comes from the 26th century, so time travel involved.
  • Argo the Ultimate Android: Duplicates super-powers.  This should be good, I asked for him earlier in the thread.
  • Hades: Literally the Greek god.  Forbidden to manipulate human affairs directly, so he has to work through agents.
  • Meta-Mind: The Grue leader, sort of an amalgam of a bunch of "evolved" grue with powerful psychic abilities.
  • Omega: Rules the Terminus (see below).  Basically Dormammu from the Dr. Strange movie (not the comic book one).
  • Freedom City: They assume you know.
  • Farside City: On the far side of the moon!  Populated by the descendants of displaced human offshoots.
  • Tartarus: From Greek mythology again.
  • The Terminus: Another dimension.  Details are lacking.  The Terminus Invasion was a major story event.

posts.cooked:
Backing was pretty much a no-brainer for me - or rather, I'd already decided to back this when the news first broke.

I love Sentinels of the Multiverse, and it is probably my favorite tabletop game (although not the one I've spent the most money on). I love Mutants & Masterminds, both the game and the world-building that's gone into the Earth-Prime setting, and I've stuck with it since I playtested the first edition some 15 years ago (holy crap). I totally understand that it's not for everyone, so that's fine. I do expect the product to turn out rather well.

posts.cooked:
I backed it. 

I'm at an odd place. I like the game design of Mutants and Masterminds. It's one of my favorite RPGs even if I don't play or run it as often as I want. I still generate characters for it whenever I'm bored. All that said, I'm only lukewarm on the setting. I like Clairemont Academy, I kinda like their heroes, I do like their villians. Honestly, I just want more options for my SOTM nights. I picked up the Cauldron once it was presented in a way that GtG got a slice of that pie as well. 

I'd say I most looking forward to Bowman as I want a more "traditional" Archer Hero deck to play. I just got Handelabra's email about what they hope to happen with the digital game. I really hope they make it happen.

massimokriya:

 I agree with you that the art of SotM is unique and has its own soul, both the earlier drawings and the latest ones. The art on show for M&M looks to me rather generic "comic superhero", drawn with greater or lesser skill and detail. I'm not even a great comic reader anymore and I still immediately recognize Namor, Captain America, the Flash, V. von Doom and a random Roman centurion : ) I just hope we get to see some cards. Even the Infernal Relics and Enhanced ed. kickstarter 5 years ago started off by showing some cards on the 1st day. If I were them, I'd also have done a small AMA here on the forums, for example. 

I really really hope they show some cards preview before the end of the campaign too. It seems that more than a few people want to know how SotM and SoEP will compare aesthetically. GtG attention to details is a very important part of why I like SotM so much…
